latitude.why: Picker vs strip, new-window vs in-place session swap, spawn-with-env vs in-process reclaim, and list ordering are all materially debatable; the ticket only sketches a direction.

q1.position: Two surfaces in the main window: a first-paint strip naming other free sessions, and a session picker overlay on Ctrl+Shift+S (listed in the help panel's Window section).
q1.rationale: Matches the ticket sketch; overlay + chord + help-row is TD's established pattern (Ctrl+Shift+A/U/D).

q2.position: Passive first: the strip appears unprompted at first paint whenever other free saved sessions exist, auto-dismissing on keypress/click. The chord-summoned picker is the persistent active route thereafter.
q2.rationale: The defect is silence; only an unsummoned surface breaks it. A chord alone requires knowledge the user provably lacks.

q3.position: Per session: id, pane count, tab count, humanized last-saved time (mtime), last_workspace hint if recorded, plus live/current badges. No titles or content previews.
q3.rationale: All derivable from scan_sessions' cheap line scan (tabs counted via [[tabs]] headers); previews need full deserialization sessions don't earn.

q4.position: Launch adopts newest as today; strip names the rest. Ctrl+Shift+S (or clicking the strip) opens the picker, arrows/click select, Enter spawns a detached TD process with TD_SESSION=<id> set programmatically; that window claims and restores it.
q4.rationale: Reuses the proven current_exe+env+setsid spawn (demo/scratch) and resolve_session's precedence-#1 path unmodified.

q5.position: New window; the current window keeps its adopted session untouched and live. No in-place replacement.
q5.rationale: One-window-per-session is TD's model; in-place swap risks the release/claim/save races #189 and #195 fought.

q6.position: Yes, exclusive: the opened window takes the existing kernel flock via claim_in. A losing race boots per existing TD_SESSION-taken behaviour (scratch, stderr notice). Picker shows advisory live badges from a non-destructive probe.
q6.rationale: The flock is already the single arbiter; adding no second mechanism means no new races.

q7.position: Strip: only when at least one other free saved session exists, so absent with zero saved or exactly one (the adopted). Picker chord always opens, showing the current session and a 'no other saved sessions' line.
q7.rationale: No false invitations at first paint; a chord that silently does nothing is the #277 bug repeated.

q8.position: Current session pinned first (badged), then the exact rank() order adoption uses: workspace-hint, then substantial, then newest, id tiebreak.
q8.rationale: One ordering rule, already tested; the list's top row explains what adoption just did.

q9.position: Strip shows at most 2 other sessions inline, then collapses to 'N other saved sessions — Ctrl+Shift+S'. Picker shows 8 rows before scrolling; all sessions remain reachable by scroll.
q9.rationale: 2 matches the ticket sketch's strip; 8 keeps the overlay one screen while covering realistic session counts.

q10.position: Stateless per launch: no new files, no new session-file fields, no persisted dismissal. Everything is recomputed from the sessions/ directory at paint and on each chord press.
q10.rationale: The file format is out of scope, and a rescan is cheap; persisted UI state would drift from disk truth.

q11.position: Yes. Strip → chord → picker → Enter completes the flow entirely in the UI; TD_SESSION is set programmatically on the spawned child, never typed by the user.
q11.rationale: This is the ticket's Done-when; the env var survives untouched as the scripting escape hatch.

q12.position: Yes, unchanged: resolve_session, rank, and claim_in are not reordered or edited on the adoption path; the strip renders after adoption completes and requires no interaction.
q12.rationale: The ticket scopes this to a UI surface over existing plumbing; #195's behaviour is the baseline, not the patient.
